origin.description: This is an example of a nested bootstrap for the correlation coefficient of the cd4 data frame. It is used in a practical in Chapter 5 of Davison and Hinkley (1997).
origin.details: Davison, A.C. and Hinkley, D.V. (1997) Bootstrap Methods and Their Application. Cambridge University Press. See also cd4.
origin.value: A bootstrap object with 999 replicates of a two-value statistic.

translation.description: This is an example of a nested bootstrap for the correlation coefficient of the cd4 data frame. It is used in a practical in Chapter 5 of Davison and Hinkley (1997).
translation.details: Saved output of a nested bootstrap for the correlation of cd4. t has 999 rows and 2 columns. t0 is the original two-value estimate. data is the cd4 table used in the fit, columns baseline and oneyear. strata and weights each have length 20. sim is ordinary and stype is w. R is 999. seed is null. statistic is the source text of the R function that produced each replicate. The saved call is boot(data = cd4, statistic = nested.corr, R = 999, stype = "w", t0 = corr(cd4), M = 249).
translation.value: A dictionary. t is a NumPy array of shape (999, 2), the replicate statistics. data is a NumPy array of shape (20, 2) with columns baseline and oneyear.
translation.example:
from boot.data_sets import cd4_nested
fitted = cd4_nested()
print(fitted["t"].shape)
print(fitted["t"][0].tolist())
